name: The body as awareness · VBT v. 63

summary.text: Verse 63 of the Vijñāna Bhairava, in Satsang’s words: rest attention on the whole body at once, the whole field of sensation, then take the body and the world around it as made of awareness; when the mind narrows to “me” and “mine”, return to the wider field.

needs_teacher_note: Safe contemplative dhāraṇā; the rest of the VBT is learned from a teacher in the Trika tradition.

steps.text: Rest attention on the whole body at once: the whole field of sensation, not one part.
Take the body and the world around it as made of awareness; felt rather than thought. When the mind narrows to “me” and “mine”, return to the wider field.

contraindications.text: If you feel disoriented, unreal or anxious: open the eyes, feel the feet and the seat, and stop for today.
A history of trauma, dissociation, psychosis or severe anxiety: keep sits short with eyes open, or practise with a qualified teacher or clinician.

value.when: if this feels unsettling: a body-based breath practice

sources.cite: Vijñāna Bhairava Tantra v. 63, summarised by Satsang in its own words; translation consulted: Christopher Hareesh Wallis, Tantra 112 (link and verse number only)
